model.name: Organizational Unit
model.purpose: Describe the internal units of an organization, including hierarchy, reporting lines, mandates, established posts, sites and structural change, independently of legal-entity identity.
model.scope_statement: This model covers an organizational unit as an internally recognized subdivision that has meaning only in the context of a parent organization. It includes how units are identified and named, how they nest, how reporting differs from containment, what remit and established posts they carry, where they are based, and how they are created, moved, merged, split or disbanded over time. It is format-neutral: directory distinguished names, RDF IRIs, FHIR resources and JSON documents are projections of the same semantics. Legal personality, employment occupancy, charters, cost-accounting objects and physical-place masters belong to sibling models.
in_scope: Internal units, departments, branches, teams, offices and similar subdivisions that are not legal entities in their own right
Preferred, alternative and former names and multilingual labels
Identifiers assigned by the parent organization's master directory, optional IRIs, and optional ISO 6523 organization-part identifiers
Classification or kind of unit within a declared scheme
Hierarchical containment, including units that contain other units
Reporting and accountability lines, including dotted-line relations, distinct from containment
Established posts that exist in a unit independently of the current holder
Head-of-unit and other membership relations at unit level
Sites, addresses and contact points of a unit
Validity intervals, active or inactive status, founding and dissolution
Reorganization events, predecessor and successor sequences, and the formal framework that prompted change
Structure-only disclosure and aggregated staffing measurements where an evidence source exists
out_of_scope: Legal-entity identity, registration numbers, LEI, DUNS and other world-facing organization identifiers of the parent body
Employment contracts, payroll, and which person currently occupies a post
Charter, statute or constitutional text as a legal instrument
Cost-centre, profit-centre and funds-centre objects as finance masters
Public-service catalogues and the services a unit delivers
Informal, shadow or purely social networks that the institution does not recognize
Physical facility, building and geospatial masters beyond the unit-to-site link
Directory-policy trees used only for access inheritance unless they also represent an institutional unit
Workforce diversity, wellbeing and other human-capital metrics that are not unit-structure facts

boundary_notes.distinction: A formal organization is recognized in the world at large, especially in legal jurisdictions, with rights and responsibilities. An organizational unit has full recognition only inside a containing organization and is not a legal entity in its own right. Every unit in this model must resolve to a parent organization; the parent is not modelled here.

A post is a position that exists independently of the person filling it and is seated in a unit. This model records that the post belongs to the unit and may record reporting between posts. Occupancy, contracts and person identity belong to the position and employment models.

A collaboration, project or consortium that spans organizations is not an internal unit of one parent. Joint or shared-service constructs should be typed as collaborations or as linked organizations, not as ordinary units, unless one parent institution actually governs them as internal departments.
FHIR Group is a collection gathered for analysis or action upon, not expected to act as an organization. A unit in this model is an institutional actor inside a parent organization.
A site is a location at which a unit exists; address components follow location vocabularies. This model stores only the link from unit to site or contact point, not the geospatial or postal master.

bundles.name: Identity and naming
bundles.description: How a unit is identified, labelled and classified without treating it as a legal entity.
bundles.rationale: Groups the findings that identify, label and classify a unit inside a parent organization without treating it as a legal entity.

layers.name: Unit identity
layers.description: Master identifiers, IRIs and part identifiers that name a unit inside a parent organization.

findings.name: Master and global identifiers
findings.description: A unit is identified first by the identifier assigned in the parent organization's authoritative directory or HR structure system. Where the unit is published as linked data, a stable IRI is a governed global identifier and should not change merely because the unit is renamed. LDAP distinguished names are naming addresses, not persistent identifiers, because reparenting changes the DN. Schema.org documents an optional ISO 6523 Organization Part Identifier (OPI) appended to an organization identifier as ICD:OID:OPI. A date is not an identifier. If no master identifier exists, the adopting Dimension assigns a UUID or ULID. FHIR requires at least a name or an identifier.

questions.text: What identifier does the parent organization's master unit directory assign to this unit, and in which scheme?
answer_data: unit-master-id (string): Identifier value in the parent organization's unit register
id-scheme (string): Scheme, datatype or issuing system of the master identifier

questions.text: If the unit is published or linked across systems, what stable IRI identifies it, and is that IRI independent of the current name and parent path?
answer_data: unit-iri (iri): Governed global identifier that remains stable across rename and reparent

questions.text: Does this unit have an ISO 6523 Organization Part Identifier relative to the parent organization's ICD and OID?
answer_data: iso6523-code (string): ICD:OID or ICD:OID:OPI form; OPI max 35 characters
opi-value (string): Organization Part Identifier component if present

questions.text: If no master-system identifier exists, what UUID or ULID did the adopting Dimension assign, and when was it assigned?
answer_data: dimension-uid (string): UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension
assigned-at (datetime): RFC 3339 assignment time with seconds and explicit offset

artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the master identifier assigned in the parent organization's unit register, then by a governed IRI, then by a Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID.

layers.name: Names and labels
layers.description: Preferred, alternative and former names of a unit.

findings.name: Lexical names
findings.description: W3C ORG recommends SKOS labels: prefLabel for the primary name, altLabel for trading or colloquial names, and notation for codes. CPOV requires at most one preferred label per language for a public organisation and allows alternative labels. LDAP requires attribute ou (organizationalUnitName) and allows description. FHIR has a single name plus aliases, including past names. Popolo adds former names as a distinct property because few vocabularies provide one. Rename does not by itself mint a new identity.

questions.text: What is the current preferred name of the unit in each relevant language, and which language tag applies?
answer_data: preferred-label (string): Primary name
language-tag (string): BCP 47 language tag

questions.text: What alternative, abbreviated or colloquial names are in use for this unit?
answer_data: alternative-labels (array): Alternative names with optional language tags

questions.text: What former names did this unit bear, and over which validity interval was each name current?
answer_data: former-name (string): Name no longer current
name-valid-from (datetime): RFC 3339 start of that name
name-valid-to (datetime): RFC 3339 end of that name if known

questions.text: If a directory projection exists, does the LDAP ou value match the preferred label, and if not, which is authoritative?
answer_data: directory-ou (string): LDAP organizationalUnitName value
authoritative-label-source (string): Which system wins on conflict

artifacts.name: Unit naming record
artifacts.description: Language-tagged preferred, alternative and former names with validity, independent of storage format
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the unit identifier together with the name value and the validity interval over which that name is current.

layers.name: Unit classification
layers.description: Kind of unit and the scheme used to classify it.

findings.name: Kind and scheme
findings.description: ORG supplies org:classification with range SKOS Concept and also allows subclassing when the kind is intrinsic. CPOV uses classification codes and points to the EU Organization Types named authority list for European institutions, while other levels must use other schemes. FHIR Organization.type is an example binding. Popolo forces a single classification per organization and requires implementations to choose one scheme. There is no universal unit-kind code list; department, branch, team, committee and similar labels are local. A committee may instead be an OrganizationalCollaboration if it is not an internal subdivision.

questions.text: What kind is this unit, in which classification scheme, and is that kind intrinsic or merely a directory grouping?
answer_data: unit-kind-code (string): Code or SKOS concept for the kind
kind-scheme (iri): Concept scheme or value set
kind-is-intrinsic (boolean): Whether kind affects other properties

questions.text: Is this body an internal unit, a committee treated as a unit, or a cross-organization collaboration?
answer_data: body-mode (code): unit, committee-as-unit, or collaboration

questions.text: May this unit carry more than one classification at once, and if a profile forbids that, which scheme is the unique classifier?
answer_data: allows-multiple-classifications (boolean): Whether multiple classifications are permitted
unique-scheme (iri): Scheme used if uniqueness is required

data_elements.description: Department, branch, team or other local kind

data_elements.name: Kind scheme
data_elements.description: SKOS concept scheme or FHIR value set

artifacts.name: Unit kind scheme
artifacts.description: Controlled list or SKOS concept scheme used by the parent organization to classify units
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the concept-scheme IRI, or by the scheme code published by the parent organization where no IRI exists.

bundles.name: Structure and reporting
bundles.description: How units nest and how accountability is drawn, including cases where those graphs differ.
bundles.rationale: Groups the findings that record containment, reporting and headship, keeping the containment graph separate from the accountability graph.

layers.name: Containment hierarchy
layers.description: Part-of relations from unit to parent organization or parent unit.

findings.name: Structural containment
findings.description: W3C ORG models hierarchical containment with subOrganizationOf and hasSubOrganization, and specializes them as unitOf and hasUnit when the child is an OrganizationalUnit. Units may contain other units. CPOV states that an Organizational Unit can exist only in the scope of its parent and cannot exist on its own, and it ranges unitOf at Public Organisation, which is narrower than ORG. FHIR models departments as Organization resources with partOf cardinality 0..1. Schema.org department links an organization to a department also described as an organization. A unit must always resolve to exactly one parent organization instance even if it also has a parent unit.

questions.text: Which parent organization instance contains this unit, and is that relationship direct or via a chain of units?
answer_data: parent-organization-id (string): WM-ORG-001 instance identifier
containment-path (array): Ordered unit identifiers from root to this unit

questions.text: Which immediate parent unit contains this unit, if any, and is more than one structural parent asserted?
answer_data: parent-unit-id (string): Immediate containing unit if not the organization root
multiple-parents-asserted (boolean): Whether more than one structural parent is recorded

questions.text: Over which interval is this containment valid, and what observation time recorded it?
answer_data: containment-valid-from (datetime): RFC 3339 effective start with offset
containment-valid-to (datetime): RFC 3339 effective end if closed
containment-observed-at (datetime): RFC 3339 ingestion or observation time

questions.text: Is this unit linked only to the legal public organisation, or is a unit-of-unit chain recorded in the ORG sense?
answer_data: hierarchy-profile (code): org-nested, cpov-flat-to-public-org, fhir-single-partof

artifacts.description: Directed part-of edge from unit to parent organization or parent unit with validity
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the child unit identifier, the parent organization or parent unit identifier and the effective start of the edge.

layers.name: Reporting lines
layers.description: Accountability relations that may differ from the containment tree.

findings.name: Reporting and dotted line
findings.description: ORG reportsTo can link agents or posts and is intended to cover both direct supervisory relations, such as objective and salary-setting authority, and more general accountability, including dotted-line reporting. Containment and reporting are different graphs: a unit may report to a unit that does not contain it. ORG does not provide a first-class enumeration of reporting kinds beyond that usage note, so a profile must record the kind. Matrix, dual-hat and dotted-line cases are in scope as reporting edges, not as extra containment parents. FHIR partOf cannot represent matrix parents.

questions.text: To which unit or post does this unit, or its head post, report, and is that edge supervisory or dotted-line?
answer_data: reports-to-id (string): Target unit or post identifier
reports-to-kind (code): supervisory, dotted-line, or other profiled kind

questions.text: Does the reporting target differ from the structural parent, and if so why is that authorized?
answer_data: reporting-differs (boolean): True when reporting target is not the container
authorization-ref (string): Decision or mandate that authorizes the split

questions.text: When did this reporting edge become effective, when does it end, and when was it observed?
answer_data: reporting-valid-from (datetime): RFC 3339 effective start
reporting-valid-to (datetime): RFC 3339 effective end if closed
reporting-observed-at (datetime): RFC 3339 observation time

questions.text: How many concurrent reporting edges may this unit or its head post carry, and which if any is primary?
answer_data: reporting-cardinality (string): Allowed concurrent edges
primary-reports-to-id (string): Primary supervisory target if designated

artifacts.name: Organization-chart reporting edge
artifacts.description: Directed reporting relation as it would appear on an organization chart, with kind and validity
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the source unit or post, the reporting target, the reporting kind and the effective start of the edge.

layers.name: Head and membership
layers.description: Leadership of a unit and membership distinct from established posts.

findings.name: Head of unit
findings.description: ORG headOf is a specialization of memberOf indicating the leader or formal head of an organization, normally the root of the reportsTo graph, though an organization may have more than one head. Membership may also be modelled as an n-ary Membership with Role and optional memberDuring interval. LDAP organizationalRole has roleOccupant. Person occupancy of the head post is an employment fact; this model records the head relation or the head post, not the employment contract.

questions.text: Which established post is the formal head of this unit, and may more than one head exist at once?
answer_data: head-post-id (string): Post that heads the unit
allows-multiple-heads (boolean): Whether concurrent heads are permitted

questions.text: Is the current head relation acting, interim or substantive, and over which interval?
answer_data: head-mode (code): substantive, acting, interim
head-valid-from (datetime): RFC 3339 start
head-valid-to (datetime): RFC 3339 end if closed

questions.text: If membership rather than a post is used, who is a member of the unit, in which role, and during which interval?
answer_data: member-agent-id (string): Agent identifier; person detail is out of scope
membership-role-id (string): Role in the membership
member-during-from (datetime): Interval start
member-during-to (datetime): Interval end

artifacts.name: Head assignment record
artifacts.description: Record that a named post or membership is the formal head of the unit for a validity interval
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the unit identifier, the head post or membership and the validity interval of the head relation.

bundles.name: Mandate and posts
bundles.description: What a unit is for and which established positions it seats, without modelling employment occupancy.
bundles.rationale: Groups the findings that record why a unit exists and which established posts it seats, without modelling employment occupancy.

layers.name: Purpose and remit
layers.description: Delegated reason for existence of a unit.

findings.name: Unit purpose
findings.description: ORG purpose documents the reason for existence of an organization and notes alternative names remit and responsibility, especially for government departments. It recommends a SKOS concept but leaves the range open. CPOV purpose is a code and recommends COFOG where possible, otherwise another controlled vocabulary. This is an alignment, not a claim that every unit has a COFOG code. Mandate text and the source of delegation are recorded here; the charter or legal instrument itself is a sibling model.

questions.text: What remit or purpose is assigned to this unit, as text and as a controlled code if one exists?
answer_data: purpose-text (string): Human-readable remit
purpose-code (string): SKOS, COFOG or other code
purpose-scheme (iri): Scheme of the purpose code

questions.text: From which decision, charter clause or parent mandate is this remit delegated, and over which interval is it valid?
answer_data: delegation-source-id (string): Reference to the delegating instrument or decision
mandate-valid-from (datetime): RFC 3339 start
mandate-valid-to (datetime): RFC 3339 end if closed

questions.text: What geographic, functional or customer-group limits constrain this unit's remit?
answer_data: spatial-coverage-id (string): Administrative region or area if constrained
functional-limit (string): Functional or customer-group limit

data_elements.name: Delegation source
data_elements.description: Charter, decision or parent mandate reference

artifacts.name: Unit mandate record
artifacts.description: Assigned remit, codes, delegation source and validity for one unit
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the unit identifier together with the purpose code or text and the effective start of the mandate.

layers.name: Established posts
layers.description: Posts that exist in a unit independently of holders.

findings.name: Posts in unit
findings.description: ORG Post is a position that exists independently of the person filling it, enabling organization charts without incumbents. A post is linked with postIn and hasPost. A post may be held by multiple people and, in some government cases, treated as an organization; ORG imposes no disjointness. Popolo requires every post to belong to an organization, distinguishes role from post, and records creation and elimination dates. Popolo rejects org:holds in favour of memberships. LDAP organizationalRole is a job, function or position with roleOccupant. Grade, pay band and establishment count are not specified by these primary sources; remuneration on ORG Role is optional and open-ranged. Occupancy is out of scope.

questions.text: Which established posts are seated in this unit, and what is each post's preferred label and role?
answer_data: post-id (string): Identifier of the post
post-label (string): Label of the post
post-role-id (string): Function the holder fulfils

questions.text: Is each post still established, when was it created, and when was it eliminated if at all?
answer_data: post-status (code): established, frozen, eliminated
post-valid-from (datetime): RFC 3339 creation or validFrom
post-valid-to (datetime): RFC 3339 elimination or validUntil

questions.text: Does this post report to another post, and is that reporting used for the unit's organization chart independently of incumbents?
answer_data: post-reports-to-id (string): Target post
chart-without-incumbents (boolean): Whether the chart is post-based

questions.text: How many incumbents is this post established for, and is that figure a local establishment control rather than a standard property?
answer_data: established-slots (integer): Planned seats if the parent records them
count-basis (string): Local basis; mark as profile extension if used

data_elements.name: Post identifier
data_elements.description: Master identifier of the established post

artifacts.name: Establishment register
artifacts.description: List of posts seated in the unit with labels, roles and validity, omitting person occupancy
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the unit identifier; each entry is identified by the master identifier of the established post.

bundles.name: Placement and contact
bundles.description: Where a unit is based and how it can be reached, without owning address or place masters.
bundles.rationale: Groups the findings that link a unit to sites and contact points without owning address, geometry or place masters.

findings.name: Unit site and contact
findings.description: ORG Site represents locations at which organizations exist, with hasSite, hasPrimarySite and hasRegisteredSite. CPOV and Schema.org attach Address and ContactPoint to organizations, including departments. FHIR distinguishes the organization hierarchy from the Location hierarchy: Locations record where a service occurs. A virtual unit may have no site. Registered site is more typical of formal organizations than of internal units. Address and geometry remain in a location model.

questions.text: At which site or sites is this unit based, and which site is primary?
answer_data: site-id (string): Identifier of a site in the location model
site-role (code): primary, registered, other
has-no-site (boolean): True for virtual units

questions.text: What contact points belong to the unit rather than to a named person, and for which purpose?
answer_data: contact-point-id (string): Contact point identifier
contact-purpose (code): Purpose such as billing, enquiry, press
email-or-telephone (string): Non-personal unit contact value

questions.text: Does the unit's site sit at a different level of the location hierarchy than the unit sits in the organization hierarchy?
answer_data: location-link-level (string): Which location node is linked
mismatch-note (string): Known offset between org and location trees

artifacts.name: Unit placement record
artifacts.description: Links from a unit to sites and contact points, omitting full address geometry
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the unit identifier together with the linked site or contact-point identifier and the site role.

bundles.name: Lifecycle and change
bundles.description: How a unit comes into being, remains valid, changes, and ceases, including rare successor cases.
bundles.rationale: Groups the findings that record validity, status, reorganization acts and successor lineage over time.

layers.name: Validity and status
layers.description: Whether a unit is in force and over which interval.

findings.name: Status and interval
findings.description: Any aspect of structure is subject to change over time. ORG says most change should be handled by an external mechanism such as named graphs, and that substantial identity change uses ChangeEvent. FHIR Organization.active records whether the record is still in active use. Popolo and Schema.org provide founding and dissolution dates. This model records an RFC 3339 valid-from and optional valid-to with explicit offset, plus a separate observation time. Status values such as active, inactive, suspended and disbanded are profile-level; mothballed and time-boxed project units are rare but in scope as status plus planned end. Reuse of a name after disbandment is why LDAP provides uniqueMember and x500UniqueIdentifier.

questions.text: What is the current lifecycle status of the unit, and is the FHIR-style record still in active use?
answer_data: unit-status (code): active, inactive, suspended, disbanded, mothballed, planned
record-active (boolean): Whether the record is in active use

questions.text: When did the unit become effective, when did or will it end, and when was that fact observed or ingested?
answer_data: valid-from (datetime): RFC 3339 effective start with seconds and offset
valid-to (datetime): RFC 3339 effective end if known
observed-at (datetime): RFC 3339 observation or ingestion time

questions.text: Has this name been reused after a previous unit was disbanded, and what disambiguator prevents identity collision?
answer_data: name-reused (boolean): Whether a prior unit used the same name
disambiguator (string): x500UniqueIdentifier, UUID or other qualifier

artifacts.name: Unit status record
artifacts.description: Current status and validity interval with separate observation time
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the unit identifier and the effective start of the status, with observation time recorded separately.

layers.name: Reorganization events
layers.description: Acts that create, merge, split, move or disband units.

findings.name: Change event semantics
findings.description: ORG ChangeEvent is a prov:Activity for a major change such as a merger or complete restructuring, intended when the resulting organization is sufficiently distinct to have a distinct identity and URI. originalOrganization, resultingOrganization, changedBy and resultedFrom relate the event to organizations. CPOV adds description, startedAtTime, endedAtTime and hasFormalFramework to legislation or policy that prompted the change. Most internal reorganizations do not mint a new URI; those should be modelled as time-qualified updates to parent, name, kind or status, optionally grouped by a reorganization act. Treating every rename as a ChangeEvent would over-claim ORG semantics. Rare cases include machinery-of-government transfers, split of one unit into several, merger without a new legal entity, spin-out of a unit into a FormalOrganization, and absorption of a former legal body as a unit.

questions.text: What kind of structural change occurred, which units were original and resulting, and did any resulting unit receive a new identity?
answer_data: change-kind (code): create, rename, reparent, merge, split, disband, spin-out, absorb
original-unit-ids (array): Units that existed before
resulting-unit-ids (array): Units that existed after
new-identity-minted (boolean): Whether a new URI or master id was assigned

questions.text: When was the change decided, when did it start to be effective, when did it end, and when was it recorded?
answer_data: decision-time (datetime): RFC 3339 decision time
started-at-time (datetime): RFC 3339 prov:startedAtTime
ended-at-time (datetime): RFC 3339 prov:endedAtTime
recorded-at (datetime): RFC 3339 observation time

questions.text: Which law, policy, board minute or reorganization notice authorized the change?
answer_data: formal-framework-id (string): Legislation, policy or decision identifier
framework-title (string): Title of the authorizing instrument

questions.text: Which affected parties must receive advance notice of this structural change?
answer_data: notice-audience (array): Units, posts or counterparties to notify
notice-required-by (string): Policy or legal basis for notice

data_elements.name: Change event identifier
data_elements.description: Master id of the reorganization act

data_elements.name: Change kind
data_elements.description: create, rename, reparent, merge, split, disband, spin-out, absorb

artifacts.name: Reorganization act
artifacts.description: Decision record that reshapes one or more units, with kind, times, original and resulting units and formal framework
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the change-event master identifier and, where present, the reference to the authorizing formal framework.

layers.name: Successor lineage
layers.description: Ordered predecessor and successor relations when identity is or is not preserved.

findings.name: Predecessor and successor
findings.description: CPOV provides prev and next so that sequences of renaming, splitting or merging public organizations can be captured. ORG derives prov:wasDerivedFrom from resultedFrom and originalOrganization when identity is distinct. Internal unit succession often keeps the same identifier; in that case prev and next describe administrative lineage, not a new legal person. Overlapping validity of predecessor and successor during a transfer window is a rare but real operating case.

questions.text: Which unit or units immediately precede this unit in administrative lineage, and do they share its identifier?
answer_data: previous-unit-ids (array): Immediate predecessors
same-identity (boolean): Whether the identifier was preserved

questions.text: Which unit or units immediately succeed this unit, and was the succession a split, merge or rename?
answer_data: next-unit-ids (array): Immediate successors
succession-kind (code): rename, split, merge, transfer

questions.text: Do predecessor and successor validity intervals overlap, and if so what dual-running rule applies?
answer_data: overlap-from (datetime): RFC 3339 start of dual running
overlap-to (datetime): RFC 3339 end of dual running
dual-running-rule (string): Which unit is authoritative during overlap

artifacts.name: Lineage chain
artifacts.description: Ordered predecessor and successor links for a unit, with succession kind and optional overlap window
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the unit identifier whose ordered predecessors and successors the chain records.

bundles.name: Measurement and disclosure
bundles.description: Evidence about staffing of a unit and the contracts under which structure may be shown.
bundles.rationale: Groups the findings that record dated staffing evidence and the contracts under which unit structure may be shown.

layers.name: Staffing evidence
layers.description: Dated measurements of established versus filled posts.

findings.name: Headcount snapshot
findings.description: ORG does not define headcount. Posts can exist unfilled, so established count and filled count are different facts. ISO 30414 is a secondary, organization-level human-capital reporting standard; its full metric definitions are paywalled and are not specified at unit grain in the sources consulted. A unit-level staffing snapshot is therefore an operating artefact many agents need, but it is a coverage gap relative to the primary organization vocabularies. If recorded, it must state basis, as-of time, observation time, and whether contractors or vacancies are included.

questions.text: As of when, how many posts were established in this unit and how many were filled, and on what basis?
answer_data: as-of-time (datetime): RFC 3339 instant the measurement refers to
established-count (number): Established posts or FTE
filled-count (number): Filled posts or FTE
count-basis (string): headcount, FTE, including or excluding contractors

questions.text: When was this snapshot observed or ingested, and which system produced it?
answer_data: observed-at (datetime): RFC 3339 observation time
measurement-system (string): Source HR or payroll system

questions.text: Must this measurement be aggregated or suppressed below a disclosure threshold before release outside the parent organization?
answer_data: aggregation-level (string): Unit, division or organization grain
suppression-threshold (number): Minimum count for release

artifacts.name: Staffing snapshot record
artifacts.description: Dated established and filled counts for one unit, with basis and observation time; treat as an extension until a primary unit-level metric standard is cited
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the unit identifier and the as-of time of the measurement, with observation time recorded separately.

layers.name: Disclosure surface
layers.description: What may be shown of structure without releasing personal or establishment detail.

findings.name: Organization chart disclosure
findings.description: ORG is designed for publishing organizational charts. RFC 4519 warns that directory entries represent real-world objects including people and that most countries have privacy laws on publishing information about people. A structure-only chart of unit names, kinds and reporting lines is a different disclosure from a chart that names heads or shows grades. Access grants belong to a sibling access model; this model must mark which findings are structure-only, which include posts, and which include measurements.

questions.text: Which projection is authorized for a given audience: structure-only chart, mandate register, or aggregated staffing?
answer_data: projection-id (code): org-chart, mandate-register, staffing-trend
audience-id (string): Partner, auditor, public or internal

questions.text: Does the authorized projection include person names or only posts and units, and under which privacy basis?
answer_data: includes-person-names (boolean): Whether individuals are named
privacy-basis (string): Legal or policy basis

questions.text: Which units are classified, embargoed or otherwise excepted from disclosure, and until when?
answer_data: excepted-unit-ids (array): Units withheld
exception-until (datetime): RFC 3339 end of exception if known
exception-reason (string): Classification or legal reason

artifacts.name: Disclosure projection
artifacts.description: Named view of structure, mandate or aggregated staffing with audience, privacy basis and exceptions
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the projection identifier together with the audience identifier for which it is authorized.

functions.name: Establish unit
functions.description: Create a new internal unit under a parent organization or parent unit, assigning a master identifier, preferred name, kind and effective time.
preconditions: The acting party is the designated establishment function of the parent organization.
The unit resolves to exactly one parent organization instance.
effects: A new unit exists under the named parent organization or parent unit from the effective time, carrying a master identifier, preferred name and kind.

functions.name: Reparent unit
functions.description: Move a unit to a different parent in the containment hierarchy without minting a new identity unless a ChangeEvent requires one. Record effective time and observation time separately.
preconditions: An effective time is supplied and, where the change is material, an authorizing framework is referenced.
effects: The containment edge points at the new parent from the effective time, and identity is preserved unless a ChangeEvent declares the resulting body distinct.
Effective time and observation time are recorded as separate timestamps.

functions.name: Merge or split units
functions.description: Combine two or more units or divide one unit, recording original and resulting identifiers, whether new identity was minted, and the authorizing framework.
preconditions: The acting party is the designated establishment function of the parent organization.
An effective time is supplied and, where the change is material, an authorizing framework is referenced.
effects: Original and resulting unit identifiers are recorded together with whether a new identity was minted and the authorizing formal framework.
Predecessor and successor lineage links are established between the affected units.

functions.name: Disband unit
functions.description: End a unit's validity, optionally preserving the identifier against later name reuse through a disambiguator.
preconditions: An effective time is supplied and, where the change is material, an authorizing framework is referenced.
effects: The unit's validity is closed with a valid-to rather than deleted, and a disambiguator protects the identifier against later reuse of the name.

functions.name: Assign mandate
functions.description: Attach or withdraw a remit, purpose code and delegation source on a unit for a validity interval.
preconditions: An effective time is supplied and, where the change is material, an authorizing framework is referenced.
effects: A remit, purpose code and delegation source are attached to or withdrawn from the unit for the stated validity interval.

functions.name: Seat post in unit
functions.description: Create or attach an established post in a unit independently of any holder. Occupancy is not performed here.
preconditions: The acting party is the designated establishment function of the parent organization.
effects: An established post exists in the unit independently of any holder, and no occupancy or employment fact is asserted.

functions.name: Assert reporting line
functions.description: Record a supervisory or dotted-line reporting edge between units or posts with validity.
effects: A supervisory or dotted-line reporting edge exists between the source and target for the stated validity interval, without altering containment.

functions.name: Disclose organization chart
functions.description: Project hierarchy, names and reporting lines for an authorized audience, omitting mandates, staffing and person names unless the grant allows them.
preconditions: An explicit grant covers the requested projection and audience; person names, grades and headcount require a separate grant.
effects: An authorized projection of hierarchy, names and reporting lines is released to the named audience, with mandates, staffing and person names omitted unless the grant allows them.

functions.name: Record staffing snapshot
functions.description: Store a dated established and filled count for a unit with basis and observation time. Treat as an extension until a primary unit-level metric standard is cited.
effects: A dated established and filled count is appended for the unit with basis and observation time, without rewriting structure.

composition.purpose: Every unit instance belongs to exactly one parent organization instance; the organization contains unit instances. Grounded in ORG unitOf and hasUnit and in the CPOV rule that the existence of a unit depends on the parent organization.

A unit instance seats or governs established position instances; occupancy of those positions is not modelled here. Grounded in ORG hasPost and postIn and in the Popolo requirement that a post belong to an organization.

Unit, containment, reporting, post, site and change-event semantics are aligned to W3C ORG, not claimed as a conformant profile unless an adopting Dimension publishes one. W3C ORG is the core reusable ontology for organizational structure and charts.

Public-sector units may align to CPOV Organizational Unit and Change Event, noting that CPOV ranges unitOf at Public Organisation. CPOV is the EU core vocabulary for public organisations and reuses ORG terms.

Healthcare deployments may project a unit as a FHIR Organization with partOf, accepting FHIR's single-parent constraint and the lack of a distinct OrganizationalUnit class. FHIR explicitly uses Organization for departments in a hierarchy.
Directory projections may use object class organizationalUnit and attribute ou; the DN is a path, not the persistent identifier. RFC 4519 is the LDAP user-schema standard derived from X.521.

owner_package_requirements: The parent organization owns the structure record; units have no standing of their own.
The custodian is the organizational-design or establishment function designated by the parent organization.
Unit records are created, changed and retired under the parent organization's authority, not by the unit itself.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Publish this model in the registry namespace vr.wm-org-002 as WM-ORG-002. Unit identifiers are namespaced by the parent organization's master directory, optionally by a governed IRI, and optionally by the ISO 6523 ICD:OID:OPI form; the W3C spelling organization is used in identifiers even in jurisdictions that spell organisation.

canonicalization_rules: Identifiers are canonicalized in the order master-system identifier, then governed IRI, then Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID; an LDAP distinguished name is a naming path, not a persistent identifier.
valid-from, valid-to, decision-time and observed-at are never collapsed into a single date field, and a date is never used as an identifier.
Containment and reporting are canonicalized as separate graphs; matrix, dual-hat and dotted-line relations are reporting edges, not additional containment parents.
patch_rules: Reparent, rename, reclassification, mandate change and reporting-edge change are recorded as time-qualified updates with an effective time and, where the change is material, an authorizing framework.
A new master identifier or IRI is minted only when a ChangeEvent declares the resulting body sufficiently distinct; otherwise name, parent, kind or status are patched in time.
Staffing snapshots are appended without rewriting structure.
compatibility_rules: Projections to W3C ORG, CPOV, FHIR, LDAP, Popolo and Schema.org are alignments only; no conformance claim is made unless an adopting Dimension publishes a profile.
A projection that cannot carry a construct, such as FHIR partOf 0..1 for matrix relations or the single Popolo classification, drops the construct rather than distorting containment.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier: Identifier assigned in the parent organization's authoritative unit directory or HR structure system
Governed stable IRI where the unit is published as linked data, independent of the current name and parent path
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension when no master-system identifier exists
Optional ISO 6523 ICD:OID:OPI organization-part identifier as a supplementary global form
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Event time and observation time are recorded as separate RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and an explicit offset, and a date is never used as an identifier.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Unit names are not serial keys: a name reused after a previous unit was disbanded receives a new master identifier or a disambiguator such as x500UniqueIdentifier, and an LDAP distinguished name remains a naming address rather than a persistent serial identifier.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every unit MUST resolve to exactly one parent organization; a unit MUST NOT be represented as a legal entity in its own right; containment and reporting MAY differ; identifiers MUST follow master-system then IRI then Dimension UUID or ULID; rename MUST NOT mint a new identity unless a ChangeEvent says the result is distinct; every structural change MUST record event time and observation time as separate RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and explicit offset.

policies: Parent-organization ownership: unit records are created, changed and retired under the parent organization's authority, not by the unit itself.
Stable identity: a new master identifier or IRI is minted only when the resulting body is sufficiently distinct; otherwise update name, parent, kind or status in time.
Structure versus people: organization-chart disclosure defaults to units, kinds and reporting lines; person names, grades and headcount require an explicit grant.
Time discipline: valid-from, valid-to, decision-time and observed-at are never collapsed into a single date field, and a date is never used as an identifier.

read: Stewards of the parent organization may read all findings.
Authorized counterparties may read a structure-only projection.
Agents may read units needed to resolve positions, mandates and routing.
create: Only the designated establishment function may create a unit, post seating or reorganization act.
Dimension UUID assignment is allowed only when the master directory has no identifier.
update: Reparent, rename, reclassification, mandate change and reporting-edge change require an effective time and an authorizing framework when the change is material.
Staffing snapshots may be appended without rewriting structure.
delete: Units are not physically deleted while successor, audit or name-reuse questions remain; they are disbanded with valid-to.
Hard delete is an exception recorded against a retention decision of the parent organization.

roles.name: Unit head post
responsibilities: Must not unilaterally alter identity or parent

roles.name: Operating agent
responsibilities: Read structure to route work and resolve posts
Must not invent units or reporting lines

access.default_rule: Deny by default except to parent-organization stewards; structure-only charts may be granted; person-identifying and staffing findings require a separate grant.
exceptions: Classified, embargoed or security-sensitive units may be omitted from all external projections until an exception expires.
Works-council, whistleblowing or legally privileged overlays are not disclosed through this model.
LDAP userPassword and any authentication secret MUST NOT be stored or projected as unit context.
audit_requirements: Create, reparent, merge, split, disband, mandate assignment and disclosure grants MUST be auditable with actor, event time and observation time.
Read of excepted units SHOULD be auditable.

coverage.claim: This model covers identity, naming, classification, containment, reporting, headship, remit, established posts, sites, validity, reorganization and disclosure of internal organizational units as specified by W3C ORG, SEMIC CPOV, IETF LDAP organizationalUnit, HL7 FHIR Organization.partOf, Popolo Organization and Post, and Schema.org department and iso6523Code. It does not claim a single global unit identifier, a unit-level human-capital metric standard, or equivalence between organization structure and finance hierarchies.

checklist.notes: Master directory identifier first, then IRI, then Dimension UUID or ULID; ISO 6523 OPI optional; LDAP DN rejected as persistent id.
Status, validity, founding and dissolution, create, reparent, merge, split, disband, spin-out and absorb, with ChangeEvent only when identity is distinct.
unitOf, hasUnit, subOrganizationOf, reportsTo, hasPost, headOf, prev, next, department and partOf alignments.
RFC 3339 valid-from, valid-to, startedAtTime, endedAtTime and separate observation time; dates are not identifiers.
ChangeEvent as prov:Activity, formal framework, original and resulting units, recorded-at distinct from event time.
Parent organization owns the record; LDAP owner is a directory projection of responsibility, not legal title.
LDAP MUST ou; FHIR name-or-identifier rule; CPOV SHACL exists for public organisations; profiles must state classification cardinality.
Structure-only versus person-identifying projections; RFC 4519 privacy warning; classified-unit exceptions.
Disband with valid-to rather than hard delete; name-reuse disambiguators; detailed records-schedule remains a sibling records policy.
Alignments to ORG, CPOV, FHIR, LDAP, Popolo and Schema.org with conflicts recorded; no conformance claim without a published profile.
org:classification and local unit-kind schemes; no universal kind list.
org:purpose and CPOV purpose including optional COFOG; charter text out of scope.
Site and contact links only; address geometry is a location model.
Unit-level established versus filled counts are operationally needed but lack a primary unit-grain standard; ISO 30414 is secondary and organization-level.

known_omissions: Cost-centre, profit-centre and funds-centre hierarchies used in ERP as parallel to supervisory structure
Typed multi-hierarchy collections such as supervisory, matrix, geographic and custom trees as first-class objects
Military table of organization and equipment versus actual strength
German works-council and other co-determination overlays
Google Workspace and other directory-policy organizational units used only for inheritance
SAP Organization-Position-Person object model as a vendor specification
ISO 30400 vocabulary definition and the full ISO 30414 and ISO 6523 texts, which are paywalled
Classified intelligence structures beyond an exception flag
Temporary project organizations as a project-management class
conflicts: CPOV ranges unitOf at Public Organisation and says a unit cannot exist on its own; ORG allows units of units and treats OrganizationalUnit as a subclass of Organization.
FHIR and Schema.org model departments as Organization with a single partOf or department link; ORG and LDAP use a distinct OrganizationalUnit class.
FHIR partOf is 0..1; matrix reporting in ORG is a separate reportsTo graph and must not be forced into containment.
Popolo allows only one classification and forbids org:holds; ORG allows multiple classifications and direct holds or Membership.
ORG ChangeEvent is for distinct resulting identity and URI; CPOV prev and next also cover rename and split sequences that may keep identity. Internal reorgs mostly should not mint new URIs.
Popolo and Schema.org use calendar dates for founding and dissolution; this model requires RFC 3339 date-times with offset.
LDAP uniqueMember encodes disambiguation in the name string; linked-data practice keeps a stable IRI and records former names separately.
regional_assumptions: W3C spelling organization is used in identifiers even in jurisdictions that spell organisation.
COFOG as a purpose code is a European public-sector recommendation, not a global requirement.
LDAP/X.500 distinguished-name trees remain a common enterprise projection but are not the semantic identity.
Legal personality follows the ORG FormalOrganization versus OrganizationalUnit split; jurisdictions that treat some departments as legal persons must type those as organizations, not units.
Privacy warnings assume jurisdictions that regulate publication of information about people.
adversarial_checks: Could a legally registered subsidiary be stored as an OrganizationalUnit and thereby lose world-facing identity? Reject: use WM-ORG-001.
Can a matrix unit with two bosses be stored with two partOf parents in a FHIR projection? Reject: one containment parent, extra reportsTo edges.
Does renaming the Finance unit require a new IRI? No, unless a ChangeEvent declares a distinct resulting body.
Does publishing an org chart that names heads process personal data? Yes; use a structure-only projection unless a grant covers names.
Is a standing committee a unit, a post, or an OrganizationalCollaboration? If it exists only inside one parent as a subdivision, it may be a unit; if it spans organizations, it is not.
Can a vacant established post keep the unit chart intact? Yes; Post exists without a holder.
If a disbanded battalion name is reused, is the new unit the same record? No; assign a new master identifier or a disambiguator.
